name: Radio group
summary: Lets people choose exactly one option from a short, visible set.
description: A radio group shows every option at once, with a legend naming the choice, and lets people check exactly one of them: checking an option unchecks the previous one. Use it when the options are few and worth reading side by side; a long list of options is a Select, and independent on/off options are Checkboxes. The group is one component: the options are its repeated part, each with its own label, description, value and disabled state.

anatomy.description: Root: the group of options (a fieldset on the web). Carries the orientation, the size and the states forced for review.
Text naming the choice. Provides the group's accessible name.
Optional help text under the legend, associated with every option as its description.
One option: its radio, label and description on a grid. Takes the states of the control it holds.

properties.name: Label
properties.description: Name of the option. Provides the radio's accessible name.

properties.name: Value
properties.description: Value submitted when the option is checked. Defaults to the option's position.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text under the option's label, exposed as the radio's description.

properties.name: Checked
properties.description: Whether this option is the chosen one. At most one option is checked.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: The option stays visible, dimmed, and cannot be chosen.

anatomy.description: The radio: the native radio button, drawn by the component. Receives focus, holds the checked state and shows it with a dot.
Text naming the option; activating it checks the radio.
Optional help text under the option's label.
Text describing the error when the group is invalid (no option chosen in a required group). Associated with every option as a description.

options.description: One option per line, the default: easiest to scan and leaves room for descriptions.
Options on one line, wrapping when needed: two or three short options (Yes / No).

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Radio size, option label and description text size scale together.

properties.name: Legend
properties.description: The question or the thing being chosen (Delivery method).

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text for the whole choice.

properties.name: Name
properties.description: Form field name shared by every option, which is what makes them one group. Defaults to the group's id.

properties.name: Error message
properties.description: What is wrong and what to do, shown when the group is invalid.

properties.name: Required
properties.description: An option must be chosen to submit the form.

properties.name: Invalid
properties.description: Validation failed: every radio takes the error border and the error message is shown.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: Disables the whole group; the chosen option stays visible.

states.description: Resting, unchecked: an outlined empty circle.
Pointer over the radio or its label. The empty circle takes a light tint; a checked radio does not change. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.
Keyboard focus on a radio. Shows the shared focus ring outside it; pointer focus shows none.
The chosen option (the entry's checked property): the circle fills with the brand color and shows a dot.
Validation failed on the group: every radio border takes the error color and the error message is shown.
Non-interactive, for the whole group or for one option (the entry's disabled property): radio, label and description drop to the shared disabled colors.

notes: The legend comes first, then the description, the options and the error message, separated by container.row-gap.
Options stack vertically, or flow on one line and wrap in the horizontal orientation, separated by container.gap for the orientation.
Within an option, the radio sits before the label, centered on its first line; the option's description sits under its label.

name.text: The group is named by its legend (the fieldset's first legend element on the web). Each option is named by its own label, associated as its label element; descriptions and the error message are exposed as descriptions of the radios, not as part of their names.

keyboard.action: Moves focus into the group, onto the checked option, or onto the first option when none is checked; the next Tab leaves the group. Disabled options are skipped.
Checks the focused option when it is not already checked.

Right or Down moves focus to the next option and checks it, wrapping from the last to the first; Left or Up moves to the previous one and checks it, wrapping from the first to the last. The browser provides this for native radios sharing a name.

guidelines.text: Expose the group, its name, each option's name and the checked state through the platform's native radio controls and grouping, so assistive technology receives them without extra work.

Use native input type=radio elements sharing one name inside a fieldset whose legend names the choice: the fieldset exposes the group role and its name, each radio its role and checked state, and the browser keeps one option checked. Never add aria-checked to a native radio.
The legend is visible and names the choice; each option has a visible label associated with its radio. Together they are the labels or instructions the group needs.
Help text and the error message are referenced by aria-describedby from every radio, so they are read as descriptions after an option's name.
Never rely on color alone: the chosen option is shown by its dot, an error is stated in text, not only by the red borders.

Legend, option labels and descriptions contrast at least 4.5:1 with the surface in every color mode and enabled state: 19.07:1 (primary text) and 12.87:1 (descriptions) in light mode, 11.27:1 and 8.80:1 in dark mode on the default surface; the error message 4.52:1 (light) and 4.97:1 (dark). Disabled text is inactive and exempt.

Each radio is what identifies its option and shows its state, so its border, its fill and its dot contrast at least 3:1 with adjacent colors in every color mode: unchecked border 12.87:1 (light) and 8.80:1 (dark) on the default surface; checked fill 5.79:1 and 12.80:1; the dot on the fill 5.74:1 and 13.04:1; the error border 6.12:1 and 3.82:1; the focus ring 5.79:1 and 12.80:1. Disabled is exempt.
A visible focus indicator appears on the focused radio, drawn outside it.
The focus ring is drawn with :focus-visible, so pointer focus shows no ring.
A radio alone is 16 or 20 CSS pixels, under the 24 pixel minimum; its label is part of the target and brings the option above it, and the spacing exception applies when options are 24 pixels apart.
When no option is chosen in a required group, say so with aria-invalid on the radios and describe the error in text; the required attribute on the radios lets the browser enforce it.

Disabling the group with the fieldset's disabled attribute disables every radio and removes them from the focus order; a disabled option uses its own disabled attribute. When people need to know an option exists, keep it enabled and explain.
Apple recommends a hit region of at least 44 x 44 pt; each option (radio and label) must reach it on iOS. Avoid relying solely on different colors to communicate the state.

Android recommends a touch target of at least 48 x 48 dp; Material's RadioButton sets that minimum itself when it can receive actions. Lift the selection to the row with the selectable modifier and the RadioButton role, so label and radio form one element whose state is announced.
Color transitions of the radios are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

guidelines: The legend is the question or the thing chosen, as a noun phrase or a short question: Delivery method, How often should we email you?
Option labels are short, parallel and mutually exclusive: Standard, Express, Pickup. Sentence case, no trailing punctuation.
Put costs, delays and consequences in an option's description, not in its label.
Order options logically (most common first, or a natural scale); offer a neutral option (None, Not sure) when people may have no preference.
The error message says what to do: Choose a delivery method.

decisions.text: The component is the whole group: a legend, optional help text, the options as a repeated part (label, value, description, checked, disabled) and an error message. On the web it is a fieldset of native radio buttons sharing one name; no single Radio component exists.
decisions.rationale: A radio button never stands alone: the choice is the group, and the native group gives the arrow-key behaviour and the one-checked rule for free.

decisions.text: The radio follows the Checkbox's selection control colors: accent neutral border on the default surface when unchecked; accent brand fill with an on-accent brand dot when checked; hover tints the empty circle with the surface hover color; invalid takes the base error border; disabled the shared disabled colors.
Options stack vertically by default, 8 px apart; the horizontal orientation puts them on one wrapping line, 16 px apart.
Two sizes: small (16 px radio, 14 px label) and medium (20 px radio, 16 px label, the default), as the Checkbox; the radio border is 1.2 px (stroke-width.md) and fully round.
